messages:
Priya Patel: Thanks everyone for coming to the all-hands. Starting a follow-up thread for process Qs we couldn't finish: release cadence, oncall rotations, quality bars, and SLA clarifications. Drop short Qs and we'll answer live in ~20m then post notes.

Alex Chen: Quick one 11 are we still running weekly release trains for hosted? Feels like a bunch of trains slipped recently.

Priya Patel: We still aim for weekly trains for hosted API. Some recent slips happened because of larger infra migrations and a couple of emergency rollbacks. We'll publish a clearer exception policy (e.g., infra migration weeks, high-impact security fixes).

Samir Gupta: For the weekly train: what's the canary length and concrete rollback thresholds? Also, do runtime-affecting PRs require the full perf suite pre-merge?

Priya Patel: Canary is 30m by default. Rollback triggers: sustained error-rate >0.5% above baseline OR p95 latency +15% sustained for 5m. Runtime-impacting PRs must have smoke perf checks passing pre-merge; the full perf suite runs post-merge and will block promotion to broader pools if it flags regressions. We also added a \"perf-test\" PR label to mark tests that need special runners.

Marta López: Oncall: several folks asked about 2-week rotations. Any firm changes?

Alex Chen: Also curious how many folks on-signal for infra vs runtime.

Priya Patel: Pilot 2-week rotations for infra teams next quarter. Runtime oncall remains 1-week for now. Typical coverage: runtime = 1 primary + 1 secondary; infra = 1 primary + 2 secondaries. We'll publish the rota, shadow policy, and escalation matrix.

Samir Gupta: Quality bars: are we enforcing a single coverage threshold across repos? PR gating rules?

Priya Patel: No global single threshold. Expect baseline: tests & CI green. Recommendations: >=60% for libs, >=80% for customer-facing/runtime-critical. Mandatory: unit tests for new logic, linters & typechecks, and for runtime touches add the perf-test label. We'll consolidate PR checklists into a short README per repo.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for train/2026-03-12 (build 2026.03.12-a9f4).

Alex Chen: Will the console show canary health per route (p50/p95/error-rate) or just a global metric?

Priya Patel: Console will show route-level p50/p95/error-rate and a canary health badge in the Releases view. We plan to surface dependent service health too. Alex, please mock the UI for the badge.

Marta López: SLA questions: hosted public SLA stays 99.9? Are there higher tiers for Dedicated?

Priya Patel: Public hosted SLA target remains 99.9. Internally we operate to 99.95 for critical infra. Dedicated customers can opt into 99.95 SLA with reserved capacity + contractual terms. We'll publish an SLA tier matrix with examples and how credits/penalties work.

Samir Gupta: Any concrete follow-ups and owners from this thread?

Priya Patel: Action items: I'll draft a one-pager with examples and thresholds. @Marta López to draft differences for hosted vs dedicated release practices. @Alex Chen to mock the console canary/route health UI. We'll add the rota template and oncall shadowing plan. Post the doc to #eng-docs and link here.

Marta López: I'll open the PR for the dedicated-vs-hosted doc by EOD tomorrow.

Alex Chen: Sharing a quick Figma mock later today and linking to the PR.

Priya Patel: Thanks all 44b We'll answer live Qs at 2pm PT and upload the recording + notes after.
